questions.subject: Deep Learning
questions.question: Explain the difference between batch normalization and optimization algorithms in Deep Learning.
questions.ideal_answer: batch normalization and optimization algorithms differ in several ways: batch normalization is internal covariate shift reduction (works by stabilizing training) whereas optimization algorithms is weight update strategies (works by adaptive learning rates). batch normalization is typically used for normalize activations, learnable scale/shift, while optimization algorithms is used for Adam, RMSprop, Adagrad, SGD with momentum. Example demonstrating batch normalization: BN(x) = gamma * (x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps) + beta. Example demonstrating optimization algorithms: Adam: adaptive moment estimation.
follow_up_questions: Under what specific circumstances would you choose batch normalization over optimization algorithms?
What is the performance or memory difference between batch normalization and optimization algorithms?

questions.question: Explain the difference between batch normalization and dropout in Deep Learning.
questions.ideal_answer: batch normalization and dropout differ in several ways: batch normalization is internal covariate shift reduction (works by stabilizing training) whereas dropout is regularization technique (works by preventing co-adaptation). batch normalization is typically used for normalize activations, learnable scale/shift, while dropout is used for randomly zeroing neurons during training. Example demonstrating batch normalization: BN(x) = gamma * (x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps) + beta. Example demonstrating dropout: nn.Dropout(p=0.5).
